mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates and boosts corporate valuation multiples, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.2 percentage point rise in unemployment rate over three months indicates accelerating labor market deterioration, triggering equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, signaling economic slowdown and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL year-over-year > 2.5%), rising inflation pressures prompt aggressive monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL year-over-year inflation exceeds 2.5%, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average indicates robust manufacturing activity and supply-side expansion, boosting corporate earnings visibility and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll decline exceeding 50,000 (PAYEMS) signals accelerating labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending capacity and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 50k in the last month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines > 50k.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate monetary tightening coinciding with economic stress, increasing recession risks and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE rises in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a quarterly GDP growth rate below 2.0% (GDPC1) signals the end of the economic cycle, triggering profit-taking and negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 year-over-year growth rate is below 2.0%, SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
